meta.title: Open Heatloss Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Open Heatloss Studio: free, open source heat loss calculation per room according to ISSO 51:2023, with an Rc calculator, PDF reports and an open IFCX file format.

header.label: Alpha · Heat loss calculation
header.title: Open Heatloss Studio
header.tagline: Heat loss per room according to ISSO 51:2023
header.desc: Calculate the design heat loss of a home room by room: transmission, ventilation, infiltration, heat-up allowance and system losses. Build up your constructions with the Rc calculator and turn the result into a PDF report. The calculation engine is written in Rust, and your project lives in an open IFCX file.

notice.text: Alpha version: the calculation engine matches three reference calculations, but the app is still in public testing. Check your results and report what you run into on GitHub.

features.label: Features
features.heading: From construction to report
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

calc.title: Every loss, room by room
calc.desc: Enter the function, dimensions, ventilation and construction elements of each room. The engine works out transmission, ventilation, infiltration, heat-up allowance and system losses according to ISSO 51:2023, and adds them up to the required heating capacity of the building.

build.title: Rc-value and vapour diffusion on one screen
build.desc: Put together a wall, floor or roof layer by layer from the material list. The Rc calculator follows ISO 6946, and a Glaser analysis shows whether condensation can form inside the construction.

report.title: A complete report in one click
report.desc: The PDF report contains the starting points, the build-up of every construction, the input and results per room, charts and the building totals. Choose which sections to include, the paper size and your own cover image.

results.title: See where the heat escapes
results.desc: The results screen shows the loss per room as stacked bars, the split between transmission, ventilation and system, and the loss per construction type. You see straight away which rooms and which parts need the most.

transmission.title: Transmission
transmission.desc: Loss through the building envelope and to adjacent rooms, neighbouring buildings, unheated spaces, the ground and water.

ventilation.title: Ventilation and infiltration
ventilation.desc: Ventilation loss with the f<sub>v</sub> factor from the 2023 erratum, and infiltration based on the qv10 of the building.

heatup.title: Heat-up allowance
heatup.desc: The extra capacity needed to get back to temperature after a night setback, per building type.

system.title: System losses
system.desc: The loss of embedded heating such as underfloor heating, also next to water, as on a houseboat.

totals.title: Room and building
totals.desc: Totals per room and for the whole building, with charts per room and per construction type.

tabs.title: Several projects at once
tabs.desc: Open projects in tabs, each with its own undo history.

library.title: Construction library
library.desc: Build-ups of walls, floors and roofs with their U-value, ready to use in any room.

rc.title: Rc calculator
rc.desc: The Rc-value and U-value layer by layer according to ISO 6946, with the correction for fasteners.

glaser.title: Vapour diffusion
glaser.desc: A Glaser analysis shows whether interstitial condensation can occur in a construction.

modeller.title: View the floor plan
modeller.desc: A 2D and 3D view of the rooms. Editing in the modeller comes in a later version.

pdf.title: PDF report
pdf.desc: Starting points, constructions, input and results per room, charts and building totals, with a table of contents.

sections.title: Put it together yourself
sections.desc: Switch sections on or off and choose A4 or A3, portrait or landscape.

layout.title: Your own layout
layout.desc: An image on the cover, your own header and footer, margins and accent colour.

tempcurve.title: Temperature profile
tempcurve.desc: A chart per construction of the temperature through the layers.

ifcenergy.title: Open file format
ifcenergy.desc: A project is an .ifcenergy file: valid IFCX (IFC5 alpha) that other software can read.

ifc.title: IFC export
ifc.desc: Export the project as IFC4X3 and view the IFC and IFCX files side by side.

mcp.title: MCP server
mcp.desc: Let an AI assistant run calculations, read project files and create reports.

api.title: REST API
api.desc: Calculate from your own software through the API of the server version.

layout.title: Report in your own layout
layout.desc: Set a header and footer with an image, the margins and an accent colour.

tabs.title: Projects in tabs

cost.q: What does Open Heatloss Studio cost?
cost.a: Nothing. The app is open source under the MIT licence and you do not need an account.

norm.a: ISSO 51:2023, the Dutch method for the heat loss of homes and residential buildings, including the 2023 erratum. Non-residential buildings according to ISSO 53 are still in development.

status.q: Can I use it for projects yet?
status.a: It is an alpha version for public testing. The calculation engine matches three reference calculations, but the app is still changing. Check your results and report what you run into on GitHub.

platforms.q: Which systems does it run on?
platforms.a: There is an installer for Windows. On a Mac or on Linux you use the browser version, or build the app yourself from the source code.

smartscreen.q: Windows shows a warning when I install it. Is that right?
smartscreen.a: Yes. The installer is not signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen asks for confirmation: choose More info and then Run anyway. You do not need administrator rights, because the app is installed for your account only.

file.a: As an .ifcenergy file. It is a valid IFCX file (IFC5 alpha), so other software can read your data. Double-click such a file in File Explorer and the app opens it.

lang.q: Which languages is the app in?
lang.a: Dutch and English. The app picks one itself, or you set the language in Preferences.

link.q: Can I connect it to other software?
link.a: Yes. Through the MCP server an AI assistant can calculate and create reports, and the server version has a REST API.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: A calculation engine in Rust with a modern interface around it, on the same foundation as the other OpenAEC apps.

rust.title: Calculation engine in Rust
rust.desc: The ISSO 51 calculation in pure Rust, tested against reference calculations.

tauri.title: Tauri 2
tauri.desc: A small desktop app with the calculation engine built in.

react.title: React and TypeScript
react.desc: The interface with a ribbon, tabs and a dark and light theme.

pdf.title: Own PDF engine
pdf.desc: Reports are laid out in Rust, with the fonts built in.

ifcx.title: IFCX
ifcx.desc: The open file format of IFC5, for projects that are not tied to one program.

mcp.title: MCP and REST API
mcp.desc: Connections for AI assistants and your own scripts.
